source: Vocabulary tab, first 50 distinct entries. Teaching content is new practice, authored for the portal.

items.meaning: Find people to join a company or group.
examples: The hospital wants to recruit more nurses.
Our club recruits new members every spring.
items.phrases: recruit staff; recruit volunteers
items.prompt: The agency's ___ helped us find an engineer.
items.task: Your café needs two new workers. Write a sentence using “recruit”.

items.meaning: Change something to improve it or make it correct.
examples: Please revise the report before Friday.
We revised our plan after the meeting.
items.phrases: revise a plan; revise a document
items.prompt: The editor asked for one final ___ of the article.
items.task: A travel plan now has the wrong dates. Write a sentence using “revise”.

items.meaning: Something that encourages someone to do something.
examples: The bonus gives staff an incentive to sell more.
Free delivery is an incentive to order today.
items.phrases: offer an incentive; an incentive to do something
items.prompt: The company offers several ___ to attract new workers.
items.task: A gym wants more people to join. Describe an incentive it could offer.

items.meaning: Put a plan or decision into action.
examples: We will implement the new safety rules next week.
The team implemented the changes in stages.
items.phrases: implement a plan; implement changes
items.prompt: Careful planning will help with the ___ of the new system.
items.task: A school has decided to reduce paper use. Write a sentence using “implement”.

items.meaning: Discuss something to try to reach an agreement.
examples: They negotiated a lower price.
We need to negotiate the delivery date.
items.phrases: negotiate a contract; negotiate with someone
items.prompt: Both sides sent an experienced ___ to the meeting.
items.task: You want a different start date for a job. Write a sentence using “negotiate”.

items.meaning: The joining of two companies into one.
examples: The merger created a larger airline.
Both companies approved the merger.
items.phrases: approve a merger; a merger between companies
items.prompt: The two small banks plan to ___ next year.
items.task: Two shops are becoming one business. Write a sentence using “merger”.

items.meaning: Money a business receives from sales before costs are taken away.
examples: Ticket sales provide most of the theater's revenue.
The café's revenue increased in June.
items.phrases: generate revenue; sales revenue
items.forms: revenues (plural, often for different sources or periods)
items.prompt: Online sales now generate half of our ___.
items.task: A museum starts selling postcards. Explain how this could affect its revenue.

items.meaning: Allowed to receive or do something because you meet the rules.
examples: Members are eligible for a discount.
You must be eighteen to be eligible to apply.
items.phrases: eligible for support; eligible to apply
items.prompt: The office will check your ___ before approving the grant.
items.task: A club gives discounts to students. Write a sentence using “eligible”.

items.meaning: Come to the end of a valid or agreed period.
examples: My passport expires in May.
The offer expired yesterday.
items.phrases: a contract expires; a card expires
items.forms: expiration (noun, US English); expiry (noun, UK English)
items.prompt: Check the ___ date on your membership card.
items.task: A discount code stops working tomorrow. Write a sentence using “expire”.

items.meaning: An arrangement that lets you pay for something later.
examples: The shop lets customers buy furniture on credit.
The bank offered the company a line of credit.
items.phrases: buy on credit; a line of credit
items.prompt: The supplier agreed to sell us the equipment on ___.
items.task: A business cannot pay for a machine today. Write a sentence about using credit.

items.meaning: A plan for how much money can be spent.
examples: Our travel budget is small this year.
We need to stay within the budget.
items.phrases: set a budget; stay within a budget
items.prompt: We are ___ for a new computer next year.
items.task: You are planning a small party. Write a sentence using “budget”.

items.meaning: The goods a business has available, or a list of those goods.
examples: The shop checks its inventory every Monday.
We have too much winter inventory.
items.phrases: check inventory; manage inventory
items.prompt: Before ordering more chairs, check our current ___.
items.task: A bookstore needs to know how many books it has. Write a sentence using “inventory”.

items.meaning: A serious disagreement, or a clash between needs or plans.
examples: The manager helped resolve the conflict.
There is a conflict between the two meeting times.
items.phrases: resolve a conflict; a conflict between
items.prompt: The two reports give ___ information about the cost.
items.task: Two teams want the same meeting room at the same time. Write a sentence using “conflict”.

items.meaning: The amount of work someone has to do.
examples: Her workload increased when a colleague left.
We shared the workload more fairly.
items.phrases: a heavy workload; reduce a workload
items.prompt: Hiring an assistant will reduce the manager's ___.
items.task: A colleague is doing too many tasks. Write a sentence using “workload”.

items.meaning: All the workers in a company, industry, or country.
examples: The factory has a workforce of two hundred people.
Training helps us develop a skilled workforce.
items.phrases: a skilled workforce; expand the workforce
items.prompt: The business plans to expand its ___ by hiring ten people.
items.task: A new factory will employ local people. Write a sentence using “workforce”.

items.meaning: A person with a senior management job.
examples: An executive approved the new project.
The company hired an experienced executive.
items.phrases: a senior executive; a company executive
items.prompt: Several senior ___ attended the board meeting.
items.task: A company needs someone to lead a new division. Write a sentence using “executive”.

items.meaning: A local office or shop that is part of a larger organization.
examples: The bank opened a branch near the station.
This branch closes at five.
items.phrases: open a branch; a local branch
items.prompt: The company has three ___ in the city.
items.task: A restaurant company is opening in another town. Write a sentence using “branch”.

items.meaning: Something valuable that a person or organization owns or has.
examples: The company sold one of its assets.
Her language skills are an asset to the team.
items.phrases: a valuable asset; company assets
items.prompt: The delivery vans are important company ___.
items.task: Explain why a helpful, experienced worker is an asset to a team.

items.meaning: Money left after the costs of a business are taken away from its revenue.
examples: The shop made a small profit last month.
Higher costs reduced our profit.
items.phrases: make a profit; increase profit
items.prompt: The new service became ___ after six months.
items.task: A shop sells more but its costs also rise. Write a sentence using “profit”.

items.meaning: The power or right to make decisions or give permission.
examples: Only the director has the authority to approve this.
The manager gave her authority over the budget.
items.phrases: have authority; authority to approve
items.prompt: We need written ___ before we can enter the building.
items.task: An employee cannot approve a large purchase. Write a sentence using “authority”.

items.meaning: Money, time, or effort used now to gain a benefit later.
examples: The new equipment was a good investment.
Staff training is an investment in the future.
items.phrases: make an investment; an investment in
items.prompt: The company plans to ___ in better training.
items.task: A bakery buys a faster oven. Write a sentence using “investment”.

items.meaning: An agreement that creates duties for the people or organizations involved.
examples: She signed a one-year contract.
The contract sets out the delivery terms.
items.phrases: sign a contract; renew a contract
items.prompt: We must meet our ___ duties to the customer.
items.task: A designer agrees to build a website for a client. Write a sentence using “contract”.

items.meaning: Start or introduce something new.
examples: The company will launch a new app in July.
They launched a service for small shops.
items.phrases: launch a product; launch a campaign
items.prompt: The product ___ attracted many customers.
items.task: A local library is starting a reading club. Write a sentence using “launch”.

items.meaning: Show that you have received something, or accept that something is true.
examples: Please acknowledge receipt of this email.
The manager acknowledged the mistake.
items.phrases: acknowledge receipt; acknowledge a problem
items.prompt: We received an ___ of our application.
items.task: A supplier tells you an order will be late. Write a sentence using “acknowledge”.

items.meaning: Say what you think will happen in the future.
examples: Analysts predict stronger sales next year.
It is hard to predict customer demand.
items.phrases: predict demand; predict a result
items.prompt: Her ___ about falling prices was correct.
items.task: A café expects more visitors during a festival. Write a sentence using “predict”.

items.meaning: A plan showing the places and times for a trip.
examples: I emailed the itinerary to the team.
Our itinerary includes two days in Osaka.
items.phrases: prepare an itinerary; a travel itinerary
items.prompt: The travel agent prepared separate ___ for the two groups.
items.task: You are visiting three cities in a week. Write a sentence using “itinerary”.

items.meaning: Needing attention or action very soon.
examples: This is an urgent request.
Please call me about an urgent problem.
items.phrases: an urgent matter; urgent action
items.prompt: We ___ need a replacement part.
items.task: A water pipe breaks in an office. Write a sentence using “urgent”.

items.meaning: Become worse in quality or condition.
examples: The road began to deteriorate after the floods.
Service quality has deteriorated recently.
items.phrases: conditions deteriorate; deteriorate over time
items.prompt: The report describes the ___ of the old bridge.
items.task: A machine works less well each month. Write a sentence using “deteriorate”.

items.meaning: Worth wanting because it is useful or attractive.
examples: Previous experience is desirable for this job.
Good transport links make the area desirable.
items.phrases: a desirable feature; highly desirable
items.prompt: The noise is an ___ feature of the apartment.
items.task: Describe a desirable feature of a place to work.

items.meaning: An amount of money given regularly or for a particular purpose.
examples: Employees receive a travel allowance.
The job includes a monthly phone allowance.
items.phrases: a travel allowance; a monthly allowance
items.prompt: Staff receive meal ___ when they work late.
items.task: A company helps staff pay for transport. Write a sentence using “allowance”.

items.meaning: A list of subjects to discuss at a meeting.
examples: Please send the agenda before the meeting.
Safety is the first item on the agenda.
items.phrases: set the agenda; an agenda item
items.prompt: We added staff training to the meeting ___.
items.task: Your team needs to discuss a new project. Write a sentence using “agenda”.

items.meaning: Money returned to someone who has paid for something.
examples: The store gave me a full refund.
You can request a refund for the canceled trip.
items.phrases: request a refund; a full refund
items.prompt: The airline ___ the cost of my unused ticket.
items.task: A customer receives a broken lamp. Write a sentence using “refund”.

items.meaning: Make certain that something happens or is true.
examples: Please ensure that the doors are locked.
Regular checks ensure safe operation.
items.phrases: ensure safety; ensure that something happens
items.prompt: The new checklist helps ___ that every order is complete.
items.task: You want all guests to receive an invitation. Write a sentence using “ensure”.

items.meaning: Send goods or people to a place.
examples: We will dispatch your order tomorrow.
The office dispatched a driver to the airport.
items.phrases: dispatch an order; dispatch a team
items.prompt: Your package was ___ this morning.
items.task: A repair company sends someone to fix a lift. Write a sentence using “dispatch”.

items.meaning: Enough or good enough for a particular need.
examples: The room has adequate lighting.
We need adequate time to finish the work.
items.phrases: adequate supplies; adequate for a task
items.prompt: All staff must be ___ trained before using the machine.
items.task: A meeting room may be too small for twenty people. Write a sentence using “adequate”.

items.meaning: A new plan for improving something, or the ability to act without being told.
examples: The city started an initiative to reduce waste.
She showed initiative by solving the problem herself.
items.phrases: launch an initiative; show initiative
items.prompt: The school introduced two new reading ___.
items.task: A worker solves a small problem without waiting for instructions. Write a sentence using “initiative”.

items.meaning: Encourage activity, interest, or growth.
examples: The discount helped stimulate sales.
The question stimulated a useful discussion.
items.phrases: stimulate growth; stimulate interest
items.prompt: We had a ___ discussion that gave us new ideas.
items.task: A town wants more people to visit its shops. Write a sentence using “stimulate”.

items.meaning: A written promise to repair or replace a product under stated conditions.
examples: The printer comes with a two-year warranty.
This repair is covered by the warranty.
items.phrases: under warranty; a warranty covers something
items.prompt: The company offers longer ___ on its premium products.
items.task: A new fridge stops working after a month. Write a sentence using “warranty”.

items.meaning: Closely connected to the subject or situation.
examples: Please include only relevant information.
Her experience is relevant to this job.
items.phrases: relevant information; relevant to something
items.prompt: The manager questioned the ___ of the old sales figures.
items.task: You are choosing examples for a talk about customer service. Write a sentence using “relevant”.

items.meaning: Look at something carefully to check its condition.
examples: A technician will inspect the equipment.
We inspected the rooms before the guests arrived.
items.phrases: inspect a building; inspect for damage
items.prompt: The restaurant passed its safety ___.
items.task: A delivery arrives with a damaged box. Write a sentence using “inspect”.

items.meaning: Start again after a pause. Here, this is the verb “resume”.
examples: The meeting will resume after lunch.
They resumed work when the rain stopped.
items.phrases: resume work; resume a meeting
items.forms: resumed (past form); resumption (noun). “Résumé” is a different noun: a job-history document.
items.prompt: Flights ___ after the airport reopened.
items.task: A class pauses because of a power cut. Write a sentence using “resume”.

items.meaning: Try hard to do something; this is a formal word.
examples: We endeavor to answer all messages within a day.
The team endeavored to improve the service.
items.phrases: endeavor to help; endeavor to improve
items.prompt: Please ___ to arrive before the doors close.
items.task: A business wants to reduce delays. Write a sentence using “endeavor”.

items.meaning: The amount by which one thing is above or below another; in business, often profit as a share of sales.
examples: The company has a small profit margin.
We included a margin for unexpected costs.
items.phrases: profit margin; a margin of error
items.prompt: Rising costs have reduced our profit ___.
items.task: A shop has little money left after paying its costs. Write a sentence using “margin”.

items.meaning: Have or own something; this is a formal word.
examples: Applicants must possess a valid driving license.
She possesses excellent language skills.
items.phrases: possess skills; possess a qualification
items.prompt: The documents are in the manager's ___.
items.task: A role needs someone with strong computer skills. Write a sentence using “possess”.

items.meaning: Keep something or continue to have it.
examples: Please retain a copy of the receipt.
The company wants to retain experienced staff.
items.phrases: retain staff; retain information
items.prompt: Better training can improve staff ___.
items.task: A club wants its members to stay next year. Write a sentence using “retain”.

items.meaning: Give money, time, ideas, or effort to help something.
examples: Everyone contributed ideas during the meeting.
The company contributes to local charities.
items.phrases: contribute to a project; contribute ideas
items.prompt: Thank you for your ___ to the team project.
items.task: You can help a community event for two hours. Write a sentence using “contribute”.

items.meaning: Something you must do because of a rule, agreement, or duty.
examples: We have an obligation to protect customer information.
The contract explains each party's obligations.
items.phrases: meet an obligation; an obligation to do something
items.prompt: Under the agreement, we are ___ to provide monthly reports.
items.task: A shop promises to replace a faulty item. Write a sentence using “obligation”.

items.meaning: Done before the main work to prepare or check something.
examples: These are only preliminary results.
We held a preliminary meeting to discuss the idea.
items.phrases: preliminary findings; a preliminary discussion
items.prompt: The team made a ___ plan before choosing the final design.
items.task: You need to check a building before planning repairs. Write a sentence using “preliminary”.

items.meaning: Make a careful guess about an amount, cost, or time.
examples: We estimate that the work will take three days.
The builder estimated the repair cost.
items.phrases: estimate a cost; estimate how long something takes
items.forms: estimate (also a noun); estimated (adjective or past form)
items.prompt: The ___ cost is lower than we expected.
items.task: You are planning a trip and do not know the exact cost. Write a sentence using “estimate”.

items.meaning: Combine things so that they work together as a whole.
examples: We will integrate the new software with our existing system.
The course integrates reading and speaking practice.
items.phrases: integrate with a system; integrate into a team
items.prompt: The ___ of the two systems took several weeks.
items.task: A company wants one system for sales and stock records. Write a sentence using “integrate”.
